panels.visual: Pericles on the Pnyx speaking to a crowd of Athenians with a raised hand, citizens voting with raised hands
panels.caption: For about thirty years, from 461 to 429 BC, Pericles was the leading man of Athens.

panels.visual: Pericles pointing at the rising Parthenon and Propylaia on the Acropolis, builders at work
panels.caption: Pericles persuaded Athens to build the Parthenon and the Propylaia.

panels.visual: A comic poet laughing on a stage as he points at Pericles' very long head under the helmet, an onion floating above, the crowd laughing
panels.caption: Comic poets joked that the helmet hid his strangely long head. They called him onion-head.

panels.visual: A crowded city in the grip of the plague, a mournful Pericles at a doorway, shadows, no bodies shown, only sorrow
panels.caption: In 430 BC a terrible plague struck. His two sons died of it, and in 429 BC so did he.
